findings.title: Retention check allows zero-day retention
findings.body: The check on line 10 allows `days == 0`, which would delete all uploads immediately. The error message claims the limit is `MIN_RETENTION_DAYS`, but the code permits zero. Reject zero explicitly or raise when `days <= 0`.
findings.suggestion:
if days <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"retention must be positive, got {days} days")

findings.title: Missing increment of removed count
findings.body: The loop on line 13 calls `delete(name)` but does not increment `removed`, so the function always returns 0 even when files are deleted. Increment `removed` inside the loop to return the actual count.

findings.title: Nightly cleanup uses 7-day retention
findings.body: The `nightly_cleanup` function hardcodes a 7-day retention (`ttl_days = 7`), which is below the minimum of 30 days enforced in `retention.py`. Either raise the TTL to at least 30 days or remove the minimum check if 7 days is intentional.

summary.problem: The retention policy allows zero-day retention, the purge function does not count deletions, and the nightly job uses a 7-day TTL below the minimum.
summary.done_well: A minimum retention threshold is introduced and enforced in the purge function.
